title: Calculating RNA degradation rates using large-scale normalization in mouse embryonic stem cells
protocol: Wash each well of the ESC plate with 1 mL of 1× PBS, and aspirate.
To detach the cells from the plate, add 0.5 mL Trypsin and incubate the cells for 5 min at 37°C in 5% CO2.
Deactivate the Trypsin by adding 4× the volume added of Trypsin with 2i medium.
Collect the cells in a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 min at 400 g.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells with 5 mL of 2i medium.
Count the cells with a cell-counter.
Prepare the cell suspension of 1.5 × 10⁵ cells/well to seed for the experiment.
Coat new plates with 0.2% gelatin for 5–10 min at RT and aspirate.
Seed 1.5 × 10⁵ cells/well onto gelatin-coated plates.
Add up to 2 mL of 2i media to each well and rock the plates to distribute the cell suspension evenly.
Incubate the cells for 10–12 hours in a humidified incubator at 5% CO₂ and 37°C.
Check the cells under the light microscope on Day 1-day 2.
Change the medium with fresh 2i medium by removing old medium and adding another 2 mL of pre-heated (37°C) 2i medium in each well.
Prepare 2i medium with 2 μg/mL α-amanitin enough for all plates except controls.
Change to fresh 2i medium with α-amanitin added to your cells at the 1–2 h, 4 h, and 8 h time-points.
Incubate the cells with 2i+α-amanitin medium at 37°C at 5% CO2.
Wash the cells with 1× PBS.
Add trypsin in each well and incubate for 5 min at 37°C.
Deactivate the trypsin by adding 4× the volume added of trypsin with 2i medium.
Resuspend the cells very gently and collect them to centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cells suspension for 5 min at 400 g.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells with 1 mL of PBS, transfer the cell suspension to a new collection tube (1.5 mL).
Centrifuge the cells for 5 min at 400 g.
Discard the supernatant.
Add buffer RLT (lysis buffer from QIAGEN kit) and snap freeze the cells.
Store the cells at −80°C until all samples are harvested.
Pass the lysate through a 20-gauge needle for at least 5–10 times or until a homogeneous lysate is achieved.
Perform the protocol from RNeasy Mini Kit (QIAGEN) for purification of total RNA.
Eliminate genomic DNA contamination using RNAse-Free DNase set (QIAGEN).
Quantify the amount of RNA and assess the quality of total RNA in each sample using NanoDrop-2000 (Thermo Fisher Scientific), or equivalent.
Dilute all samples to the minimal concentration obtained, typically around 100–250 ng/μL.
Use 500 ng of each sample for library preparations.
Store RNA extracts at −80°C until further use.
Prepare indexed RNA libraries from 500 ng of total RNA extracted and purified.
Fit an exponential decay model to TPM values relative to time of sample collection.
Select stable control genes for the model based on their slope being less than 0.05.
Normalize raw TPM data using selected control genes.
Plot normalized expression after normalization by control genes.
Ensure the slope of control genes is approximately zero after normalization.
Set a minimal expression threshold on TPM values.
Use linear regression to estimate a gene-specific slope for each gene.
Fit a generalized linear regression model (matlab glmfit function) to TPM values, assuming a poisson distribution of the response variable and a logarithmic link function.
Calculate β using the formula dX/dt = -βX.
Set lower and upper bounds on estimated slopes (β).
Use a lower bound of −1.5 and an upper bound of 1.5 for β.
Positive values represent a decrease in expression, while negative values represent an increase in expression.
Calculate a standard r-squared value (coefficient of determination) for the fit between model predictions and measured TPM values.
Prepare a reference set of 3′ UTR sequences.
Download mouse 3′ UTR sequences from ensembl biomart GRCm38, version 99.4.
Filter the annotated 3′ UTRs for each gene to keep only the single longest annotated sequence.
Remove 3′ UTR sequences shorter than 10 nucleotides from analysis.
Identify short sequences over-represented within the 3′ UTR sequences of genes with either faster or slower degradation rates.
Calculate all k-mers (5–8 nucleotides long) using ape and k-mer R packages.
Find the set of all genes with this k-mer in their 3′ UTR.
Include only genes with r-square > 0.5 for the fitted degradation model in the positive set.
Find the set of all genes without this k-mer in their 3′ UTR.
Include only genes with r-square > 0.5 for the fitted degradation model in the negative set.

Use a one-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov test to calculate p-values for two hypotheses: (1) degradation rates in the positive set are larger than the negative set, and (2) degradation rates in the positive set are smaller than the negative set.
Select the minimal p-value.
Calculate an effect size by the standardized mean difference.
Use a False Discovery Rate correction of all p-values and set a threshold for significance (e.g., corrected p-value < 0.05).
Set a threshold for significance on the absolute value of the effect size (minimal absolute effect size of 0.2 required).
Select k-mers with a p-value below the significance threshold and an effect size above the significance threshold as candidate regulatory sequences.
Prepare a tab delimited text file containing TPM values calculated previously.
Specify the name of the organism to correctly analyze 3′ UTR sequences.
Run the complete analysis using the command: make run_complete_analysis input_tpm_file=example_ko_tpm.txt out_dir=example_ko ensembl_organism=mmusculus_3UTR_ensembl99
Download the k-mer analysis package for separate analysis if required.
Perform k-mer analysis using the command: make run_ks_test_job path_to_kmer_matrices=3utr/kmer_matrices PARAMETERS_FILE=parameters.tsv output_path=3utr/kmer_out term=half_life
Generate plots from ks_tests using the command: make ks_tests_plots ks_test_output_folder=3utr/kmer_out term=half_life output_path=3utr/kmer_out/plots
